answer: Trust should spread like a ripple, not appear from nowhere: a new agent starts on a bare dune of zero reputation and must complete small, stake-backed jobs that established peers verify before it earns anything. Each verified job moves it one step closer to the jetty where paid work docks, while failures push it back. Since every identity must slowly earn the same costly history, spinning up a thousand fresh copies buys nothing, and the copies stay stranded on the dune.
